newsitem.title: MEXICO: Sole bidder remains for Mexico's Ensenada port.
newsitem.headline: Sole bidder remains for Mexico's Ensenada port.

text.p: Three of four firms vying for 20-year operating rights at Mexico's Pacific coast port in Ensenada, Baja California state, have dropped out of the bidding, Communications and Transport Ministry officials said Tuesday.

Only Philippine company International Container Terminal Services Inc. and bidding partner Empresas ICA will remain in the bidding, a spokesman for the ministry told Reuters. The venture's plans for the port and its price offered are scheduled for release by March 13.
He said the ministry was not told why the other companies dropped out of the bidding.

Other former bidders as of last week, were Transportacion Maritima Mexicana (TMM) with Servicios en Puertos y Terminales and Operadora Portuaria de Ensenada, Internacional de Contendores Asociados de Veracruz and a joint venture between Grupo Morphy and MAP Services, LTD.
"We analyzed the situation and see a lot of future potential in the medium and long term, but currently we prefer to concentrate on other projects," TMM spokesman Fernando Ruiz said.

Ensenada is a multi-use, commercial, fishing and tourist port in the northwest of the Baja California peninsula. It ranked second in the country in cruise tourist traffic and sixth in cargo traffic in 1993.

The port is said to require infrastructure investments, such as a railway line connecting transport cargo to major consumption centers, to make it more competitive with nearby San Diego port in California.

Mexico is auctioning operating rights to its ports and other transport assets. The privatizations have been clouded by investor doubts about the profitability of the assets. The government has sought to make the process fully transparent.
